stories.title: Big Four firms expand Indian deal teams
stories.summary: The Big Four are expanding their Indian M&A and transaction advisory businesses to capture a local dealmaking boom. EY now counts over 300 partners in its local deals unit, while Deloitte, PwC and KPMG have also scaled their teams to handle billions in annual transactions.

stories.title: KPMG consulting head says clients want outcomes but still compare hourly rates
stories.summary: KPMG global consulting head Svilena Tzekova says AI has made much paid advice work effectively nonexistent. Despite this, procurement departments continue to compare bids by headcount and hourly rates. Clients are seeking new outcomes while remaining attached to the traditional billable hour.

stories.summary: At least four senior tax executives have left Deloitte East Africa to join rival KPMG. The departures follow strategic disagreements at the firm, highlighting the ongoing competition for talent among the Big Four accounting networks in the region.

stories.summary: EY Australia has launched an Oceania Public Interest Council with a majority of independent members to strengthen its governance. The move comes as Australian regulators consider tougher requirements for accounting firms, following warnings that previous independent inquiries failed to uncover evidence of misconduct.

stories.title: McKinsey warns of air travel slowdown
stories.summary: More than half of airlines expect an air travel slowdown over the next two to three years, according to a McKinsey report. Rising jet fuel prices, maintenance costs and aircraft delivery delays are cited as primary factors weighing on the industry growth outlook.

stories.title: 56% airlines foresee air travel slowdown in 2-3 years: McKinsey
stories.summary: Over half of airlines expect an air travel slowdown in the next two to three years due to rising jet fuel prices, maintenance costs, and aircraft delivery delays, a McKinsey report says. stories.title: McKinsey warns companies remain exposed to trade chokepoints
stories.summary: McKinsey says the global economy remains vulnerable to shocks at key shipping passages like the Strait of Hormuz. The firm frames these chokepoints as a standing liability for corporate earnings, noting that a single blockage can strand components and force factories to cut shifts.

stories.title: TCS study finds AI productivity gains met with workforce uncertainty
stories.summary: A study by Tata Consultancy Services suggests that while AI drives productivity, business leaders are increasingly uncertain about how to reshape job roles around the technology. Expectations for AI appear to be tempering as the reality of implementation continues to evolve.

stories.title: LEO Pharma to acquire dersimelagon rights from Tanabe for $435m
stories.summary: LEO Pharma, which describes itself as a global leader in medical dermatology, is acquiring rights to the drug dersimelagon from Bain-owned Tanabe for $435 million. The company currently serves nearly 100 million patients annually across more than 70 countries.

WHI Holdings eyes $2.5 billion valuation for Tokyo IPO
stories.summary: Human resource systems developer WHI Holdings is scheduled for a December 15 initial public offering in Tokyo. The private equity-backed company is expected to reach a valuation of roughly 400 billion yen, or $2.5 billion, marking what would be Japan's largest listing of 2026.

eClerx acquires consulting firm RegEdge
stories.summary: eClerx has acquired RegEdge, a U.S.-based consulting firm specializing in financial services risk management and regulatory compliance. The acquisition adds expertise in transaction reporting and compliance transformation to the company's existing portfolio of AI-powered analytics and business process management services. Financial terms were not disclosed.

BRG adds three experts to US offices
stories.summary: Management consulting firm BRG has hired Punam Anand Keller as a senior advisor, alongside Marcus Leach and Josh Hesterman as managing directors. Keller, a faculty member at the Tuck School of Business, joins the firm's consumer protection and product liability practice to support ongoing litigation efforts.

stories.title: NITI Aayog reports on PLI scheme progress
stories.summary: A NITI Aayog assessment of India's 14 Production Linked Incentive schemes reports 849,069 jobs created against a target of over 3 million. Advanced chemistry cell battery capacity has reached 1.4 GWh of a 50 GWh goal. A government think tank auditing its flagship programme this candidly is itself.

stories.title: NITI Aayog releases impact assessment of PLI schemes
stories.summary: NITI Aayog has released an impact assessment of the government's Production Linked Incentive schemes, prepared with the Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad. The report describes the policy as a flagship intervention designed to enhance manufacturing competitiveness and accelerate the journey toward an Atmanirbhar Bharat.

stories.title: NITI Aayog finds PLI schemes hit 28 percent of job target
stories.summary: India's 14 production-linked incentive schemes generated 849,069 jobs by fiscal year 2026, reaching 28 percent of the 3 million target. While investment reached 76 percent of its goal, the policy think tank has called for design changes to improve the schemes' overall effect.

stories.title: PLI schemes reach 28 percent of employment target
stories.summary: India's production-linked incentive schemes have generated 849,069 jobs against a 3 million target by fiscal year 2026. While investments reached 76 percent of the 3.15 trillion rupee goal, the findings highlight the difficulty of converting manufacturing expansion into large-scale job creation.

stories.title: NITI Aayog assessment calls for PLI scheme redesign
stories.summary: A new NITI Aayog assessment reveals that India's Production-Linked Incentive schemes met 28 percent of their employment target by fiscal year 2026. The report suggests a strategic shift toward demand-side support, noting that investment mobilization reached 76 percent of its target while production reached 64 percent.

stories.title: NITI Aayog notes uneven MSME gains in PLI schemes
stories.summary: A NITI Aayog report indicates that while PLI schemes have boosted investment and exports, benefits for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises remain uneven. The assessment cites constraints in scale, technology, and market access as primary factors limiting participation for smaller firms across the 14 sectors.

stories.title: NITI Aayog publishes mid-course PLI impact report
stories.summary: NITI Aayog has published a mid-course report evaluating all 14 Production Linked Incentive schemes. Developed with the Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad, the assessment measures performance across investment, production, employment, and export outcomes to support the government's Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat initiatives.

stories.title: PLI incentive disbursements reach 18.5 percent of outlay
stories.summary: A joint assessment by NITI Aayog and IIM Ahmedabad found that cumulative disbursements under India's 14 PLI schemes reached 18.51 percent of the total approved outlay by March 2026. The report recommends reforms to improve the long-term effectiveness of the 1.91 lakh crore rupee program.

stories.title: ACC battery scheme faces capacity gap
stories.summary: The ACC battery PLI scheme has created 1.4 GWh of manufacturing capacity against a 50 GWh target, with commercial production yet to begin. The report notes that building a domestic battery ecosystem remains difficult when technology, raw materials, and supply chains must develop simultaneously.

stories.title: Accenture India announces performance bonuses
stories.summary: Accenture has rolled out performance-linked bonuses for Indian employees ranging from 8 to 26 percent for the November 2026 cycle. While top performers receive payouts, those classified as non-performers receive nothing. The company currently employs 3.5 lakh people in the country, representing nearly half of its global workforce.

stories.title: Accenture India links pay to performance as hikes remain on hold
stories.summary: Accenture has issued performance bonuses of up to 26 percent for Indian staff in its November 2026 rewards cycle. While eligible employees receive payouts based on performance tiers, annual salary increments and promotions remain largely on hold. The company continues to manage its staggered compensation framework across career levels.

stories.title: Accenture rolls out bonuses
Accenture Rolls Out Up To 26% Performance Bonus For Top Employees, Salary Hikes Remain On Hold - News18
Accenture India rolls out bonuses of up to 26%, salary hikes largely on hold - Moneycontrol.com
Accenture freezes salary hikes while issuing performance bonuses
stories.summary: Accenture has announced performance-based bonuses of up to 26 percent for top-performing employees in India. While the November 2026 rewards cycle provides payouts for those meeting performance criteria, annual salary raises remain largely frozen and promotions are restricted. Performance is now the primary variable in the compensation equation.

stories.title: PwC US launches critical thinking certification for staff
stories.summary: PwC US is introducing a critical thinking and judgement certification for its 85,000 employees. The firm notes that as AI tools take on research and writing tasks, junior staff have fewer opportunities to develop professional judgement through traditional assignments. The machine is learning, so the humans must certify.
